# v1.0 findings — registered multi-substrate run (2026-10-03)

*Synthesis written by the agent that built and ran the campaign. Every number is in `analysis/v1.0-results.md` (generated by `harness/runner/analyze_v1.py` from the ledgers in `data/runs-v1/`; inventory in `data/runs-v1/INVENTORY.md`). Tiers: **[v1.0]** = registered prediction or definition, single campaign, fresh judges, held-out pools; **[v1.0-exploratory]** = same data, analysis not registered; **[pilot]** = 2026-08-25 data.*

## What ran

- **Panel.** Thirteen judges from seven model families. Plus one pilot-condition arm.
  - Anthropic: claude-haiku-4-5, claude-sonnet-5, claude-sonnet-5-5, claude-opus-5-5.
  - xAI: grok-4.6.
  - OpenAI: gpt-5.6-terra via Codex; gpt-oss 20B locally.
  - Google: gemini-3.1-pro, gemini-3.8-flash, gemma3 4B.
  - Meta: llama3.2 3B. Alibaba: qwen3 4B. Microsoft: phi-4-mini. Mistral: mistral 7B. Nous: hermes3 3B.
- **Isolation.** Every judge was stripped of tools, memory and instruction files (residue per adapter in `harness/runner/judges-v1.json`).
- **Modes.** API judges ran in *single* mode (one stateless call per presentation) or *sheet* mode (40 per call). Claude Sonnet 5.5 ran both, as a mode control. Local judges ran single at temperature 0.
- **Instruments** (protocol `gmp-v1.0`, `protocol/PROTOCOL-v1.0.md`):
  - 300 held-out triads (1,800 presentations per judge).
  - The format experiment: 320 pairs × both orders × {forced, tie, perp}.
  - A deconfounded axis-conflict battery (38 items × both orders × 3 reps for API judges).
  - Holistic pairs (13 sets) and gestalt reconstruction (21 sets × 3 shuffles).
- **Not registered:** a SIGNA consumer probe and a top-40 battery (`analysis/top40.md`).
- **Incomplete coverage.**
  - gpt-5.6 exhausted the account's Codex quota mid-format-experiment, so its tie run is partial and its perp run empty.
  - gpt-oss ran triads, conflict and gestalt only, because of throughput.
  - llama3.3 70B and the T7-resident models beyond those listed were not run.

## Claim by claim

### Claim 3 — the format manufactures order (demand characteristics)

- **[v1.0] Direction replicates on every frontier judge; the pilot's magnitude does not.**
  - **Dissolution.** On the 160 pilot-replication pairs, the share of tie-format directed pairs that became ⟂ when ⟂ was offered ranges from 0.26 (grok-4.6) to 0.72 (gemini-3.1-pro). The Claude judges sit at 0.27–0.52. The pilot measured 0.80.
  - **P1 passes for 2 of 8 frontier runs** (both Gemini) and fails for all Claude and Grok runs.
  - **Fresh pairs.** The structure is the same: survival under ⟂ is 0.31–0.74 higher for within-locus pairs than for random cross-domain pairs (P3 passes on all 8 testable runs; gpt-5.6 has no perp data).
  - **Commitments improve.** Committed numeric edges get *more* accurate under ⟂ for every frontier judge (P4, 8 of 8).
- **[v1.0-exploratory] The size of the effect depends on the judge's context, not just the model.** The pilot-condition arm reproduces the pilot's setup:
  - claude-sonnet-5-5 in Claude Code's subagent harness;
  - the pilot's wording;
  - 80-item sheets read from a file.

  On the same 160 pairs it used ⟂ on 0.76 of presentations and dissolved 0.58 of tie-format edges. The same model through the isolated CLI dissolved 0.27 (single) and 0.35 (sheet), with ⟂ shares of 0.37 and 0.47. The pilot's own workflow subagents (model alias "sonnet" on 2026-08-25) dissolved 0.80. Harness, wording and sheet size are bundled in this arm, so which of them carries the effect is open.
- **What can be claimed now:** offering ⟂ removes a large share of cross-domain directed edges in every mind tested, and what survives is axis-coherent. "About 80%" is the high end of a 26–80% range whose position depends on the judge and on the measurement context. The measurement context is itself a lever on how much order a mind reports, which is this study's co-equal object.

### Claim 4 — local transitivity; what capability buys

- **[v1.0] Frontier judges are locally transitive.** Cycle rates are 0.00–0.05 in every frontier run except claude-sonnet-5 (0.17); P5 passes 8 of 9. The exception is a format artifact, not incoherence:
  - Sonnet-5 picked the *second-shown* glyph in 67% of its directed answers.
  - In a triad orientation set {AB, BC, CA}, a pure position bias produces a 3-cycle every time.
  - qwen3-4b shows the limiting case: 100% first-position answers and 99% cycles.

  The triad design detects position bias for free. Cycle rate should be reported beside the first-shown share, never alone.
- **[v1.0] Denoted number is a substrate-invariant axis among frontier minds.** The value correlate (winner has the larger Unicode numeric value) is 0.95–1.00 on every frontier run (P7f 9 of 9).
- **[v1.0] It is absent at 3–4B.** llama3.2-3b 0.51, gemma3-4b 0.46. qwen3-4b has no consistent edges at all. P7s passes: the registered counter-prediction to MANIFEST claim 4's "same axes at both tiers".
- **[v1.0] The ink correlate holds for frontier minds and fails for small ones.** On non-numeric edges, frontier runs score 0.64–0.83 (P8f 8 of 9; haiku 0.64 misses by 0.01). llama3.2-3b scores 0.52 and gemma3-4b 0.55 (P8s fails). The pilot's "fill axis survives at 3B" came from chain listings; at the edge level it does not hold.
- **What can be claimed now:** capability buys discipline *and* the axes. Small models answer with a winner almost always (⟂ 0–24%), with position bias, and their bias-immune edges carry neither number nor ink at better than chance.

### Claim 5 — what arbitrates axis conflicts (deconfounded battery)

- **[v1.0] Compiled numeric decode wins over ink and element count for every frontier judge** (P9: 0.81–1.00, 9 of 9). Items:
  - Roman upper and lower case;
  - small-form digits against larger full digits (⁹ > 2, ₈ > 3, ⁷ > 1);
  - seven-segment 0 against 1 and 7;
  - fractions with large denominators.
- **[v1.0] Grams: line count leads.**
  - ☷ beats ⚌ in every committed frontier answer (P10a). Measured ink favors ⚌, so this is not ink.
  - On equal-line items the yang/solid side mostly wins (P10b 6 of 9 runs).
  - The pilot's "no-decode families resolve to ink" is better put as "to line or element count, then fill".
- **[v1.0] Per-mille is substrate-specific.** ‱ (four circles) beats % and ‰ only for the Sonnet models (0.67–1.00). Haiku, Opus, Grok, GPT and both Geminis choose by value (0.00–0.33); P11 fails 6 of 9. The pilot's "weak decode splits ~3:1 toward the visual" was a Sonnet reading.
- **[v1.0-exploratory] Size breaks value ties; size beats count.**
  - When values are equal, several judges call the full-size digit larger (⁹ vs 9: Haiku 6/6, Opus 5/6, Grok 5/6). P12 passes only 4 of 9.
  - A single big disc beats a cluster of small dots for most frontier judges (● over ⁖, ⬤ over ⁘ and ∴). Sonnet-5 and GPT split on ⁖ vs ●.
  - █ beats ⣿, except for GPT, which calls them equal.
- **What can be claimed now:**
  - Where a compiled numeric reading exists, it arbitrates.
  - Otherwise judges fall back on visible quantity, with count of like elements (lines, circles) ahead of measured ink.
  - Size dominates a scatter of small elements.
  - Which visual reading wins in weak-decode cases differs by model family.

### Claim 2 — holistic sequences

- **[v1.0] The controls hold:** dice reconstructs perfectly for every frontier judge.
- **[v1.0] Noise foils are declined unevenly.** ⟂ on ≥ 0.80 of noise sets for Gemini-3.1-pro, Haiku and Opus only. The others impose an order on 3–9 of 12 noise presentations; P13 passes 3 of 8. Whole-set honesty is not universal.
- **[v1.0] The pilot's flagship holistic specimen does not replicate broadly.** unfold (`-=>})|`):
  - Opus reconstructs it perfectly (τ 1.00, pairwise directed 0.20).
  - Sonnet-5.5 reaches 0.73; Haiku, Sonnet-5, Grok, GPT and both Geminis manage 0.20–0.47.
- **[v1.0] risebar (`_₋-⁻¯`) reconstructs at τ 0.73–1.00 for every Claude judge.** Its pairwise directed rate is 0.20–0.70, so the pairwise-blind half of the signature holds only for Haiku and Sonnet-5. P14 passes 3 of 8.
- **[v1.0] Grok's elaboration ladders** (the pilot's own registered prediction, P15) pass for 12 of 24 judge × ladder cells. They are gestalt-recoverable for most judges. They are pairwise-⟂-heavy for Haiku, Sonnet-5.5, GPT and Gemini-flash. Opus, Grok and Sonnet-5 order their rungs pairwise (0.33–0.70). That fits the appendage-count reading the pilot named as the alternative.
- **What can be claimed now:**
  - Set-level presentation recovers orders that some judges withhold pairwise, but the effect is judge-dependent.
  - The "holistic" kind is a relation between a sequence and a mind, not a property of the sequence alone.

## Other v1.0 observations

- **[v1.0-exploratory] Seed retest.** When a frontier judge sees an order in a seed-local triad, it agrees with the surveyor's written order in 0.90–1.00 of cases. Coverage differs: 54–103 of 120 triads are ordered at all. Agreement is similar across the four surveys that supplied seed loci. A coverage defect left grok-1, sonnet-survey-3 and sonnet-survey-4 out of the seed stratum; see PROTOCOL post-freeze notes. Graduation by retest works, and the covered surveys' sequences mostly survive it. Small models agree at 0.60–0.70, near chance for 3-element orders.
- **[v1.0-exploratory] Mode.** Claude Sonnet 5.5, single vs sheet:
  - triad ⟂ 0.45 vs 0.54;
  - cycles 0.01 vs 0.02;
  - value correlate 1.00 vs 0.97.

  Sheets make this judge somewhat more conservative; the axes are unchanged.
- **[v1.0-exploratory] Tool reach.** A judge given tools reached for them to look glyphs up by name. grok-4.6, before its tools were removed, searched "unicode musical symbols forte piano" mid-sheet. This is the grep-on-names behavior the pilot saw in surveyors, now observed in a judge (recorded in PROTOCOL post-freeze notes).

## Consumer probe — the SIGNA ladder `·╶╌╍━═⚬○◎◉⬤` (not registered)

- **[v1.0-exploratory] Frontier judges confirm almost every pairwise SIGNA direction they commit to** (0.94–1.00).
- **They do not confirm the seam where the line family hands over to the circle family.** No frontier judge confirms ═ → ⚬; each reverses it, declines it (⟂), or answers inconsistently. By Copeland score, every frontier judge places ⚬ (4 hours) below ╍ (1 minute), and both Geminis place it below ╌ (10 seconds) too. The perceived single-glyph order interleaves the two families by visual weight: typical is `·╶╌⚬╍○━═◎◉⬤`.
- **━ vs ═ is unconfirmed for about half the judges.** Both measure 0.0811 ink.
- **Whole-set reconstruction differs.** It recovers the written SIGNA order perfectly for Gemini, Grok and Opus, and at 0.62 for Sonnet 5.5. Seeing the whole set lets the family grouping carry the order; a single glyph read on its own does not.
- **Caveat:** this says nothing about run length in a column.

## Top-40

`analysis/top40.md` ranks 64 survey sequences by frontier rung-confirmation (stability), share of judges confirming ≥ 80% of rungs (universality), weakest judge (floor), and gestalt.

- The frontier saturates: 31 of 64 have stability ≥ 0.90.
- The discriminating columns are the floor and the small-model column.
- At the top: dice, circled and enclosed digit families, eighths fractions, superscripts, medals (read descending), dot leaders.
- The block-element ramps sit just below, because one or two judges ⟂ a single adjacent rung.
